observation.visible_scene: A right hand pinches a Staples CD-RW optical disc (label side facing the camera) above a dark wooden tabletop; a green Staples CD-RW jewel case sits in the lower-left corner throughout. The camera viewpoint and the background/jewel-case positions remain fixed.
visible_changes: For roughly t=0 to t≈1.87 s the disc is held label-side front with only small, slow tilts and rotations; the printed 'STAPLES CD-RW' text stays legible and the rainbow sheen on the label drifts across the surface as the angle changes.

From about t≈1.94 s the hand tilts the disc more strongly toward the light, so the label washes out into a bright overexposed glare (most pronounced around t≈2.0–2.14 s) and the disc's apparent shape foreshortens from a full circle toward an ellipse.
Around t≈2.34–2.40 s the disc passes nearly edge-on (a thin sliver), then continues rotating to reveal its reflective data side.

From t≈2.47 s to the end the shiny mirror/data face of the disc fills the view, showing strong spectral rainbow diffraction bands over a dark reflective surface; the hand's grip (thumb at lower right, fingers at top) is maintained.
The jewel case in the lower-left and the wood-grain background do not move relative to the frame, indicating the change in view is object motion (disc tilt/flip), not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What precedes the held pose and what follows the data-side view (e.g., whether the disc is placed in a drive or returned to the case).
The cause of the bright glare (light-source position) and the identity of the person.
Whether the small label-side wobble is intentional inspection or just hand tremor.
uncertain_details: Exact moment the flip begins is gradual rather than a single frame; the edge-on orientation is brief and motion-blurred.
Minor apparent size changes of the disc are due to tilt/foreshortening, not translation toward or away from the camera.
The hand's slight repositioning relative to the disc during the steady phase is small and hard to attribute to either hand or disc motion.
